rows.original:
"Don't raid the Marches," you say.
    
    "Aaaahh, but they've got the best fights!" Maidensbane hisses, slapping a hand to her forehead in dismay. "Gah... ye bastard. I'll be fightin' ye again t'get that right back, I will."
    
    "As long as you uphold the deal," you say.
    
    "Yer not the first to have tried it, but yer the first to have won. We're stuck here for the time bein' so there's nothin' to be done on that end, but the duels are sacred. T'would be a fool pirate that broke the vow under Tira's watchful eye." She shakes her head. "Earns ye a murky grave sooner rather than later."
    
    "Would be a shame, too," she adds. "The bulls 'n orcs always put up a good, hard fight."
rows.translation:
“别去劫掠边境地区，”你说。
    
    “啊——可那儿有最精彩的架打！”少女克星恼怒地嘶声道，绝望地一巴掌拍在自己额头上。“啧……你这混蛋。我一定会再跟你打一场，把那些地方夺回来，我说到做到。”
    
    “只要你们遵守约定，”你说。
    
    “你不是第一个这么试的人，但你是第一个赢的。眼下我们被困在这儿，那方面没什么办法，不过决斗是神圣的。在蒂拉的注视下违背誓言，那得是个蠢到家的海盗。”她摇了摇头。“那只会让你更早进坟墓，还是座浑水坟。”
    
    “那也太可惜了，”她补充道。“公牛和兽人总是能打一场又硬又漂亮的好架。”

rows.original:
You inspect the robes, taking the hem in your hand. They're made of fine cloth, dyed purple and yellow, almost gold, and there's a faint sensation of magic lingering in the threads.
    
    "What is this?" you ask.
    
    "Some artifact," Maidensbane says. "Never worn 'em. Came from a raid on some ship carrying Velunites. They weren't happy about it."
    
    Velunite ceremonial robes? Perhaps they empower natural magic or something of the like. It's impossible to be certain without trying them on.
rows.translation:
你仔细端详着那些长袍，用手摸了摸它们的下摆。它们由质地精美的布料制成，被染成了紫色和黄色，近乎金色，而那些丝线中似乎还萦绕着一丝神秘的力量。
    
    “这是什么？”你问道。
    
    “是一些古老的遗物吧，”少女克星回答道，“从来没人穿过它们。这些长袍是在一次袭击某艘运送维伦信徒的船只时获得的，那些维伦信徒对此可不太高兴。”
    
    维伦信徒的仪式用长袍？或许它们能增强自然魔法之类的能力吧。不过不试穿一下的话，也很难确定。

"That one’s nice and simple," Maidensbane says as you reach for it. "Magically enchanted. Someone hits it while yer holdin’ it, hurts them just as bad as it’d be if they hit you."
    
    "A reflection spell?" you say.
    
    "Nothing as fancy as shooting spells back, but somethin’ like that," she says.
    
    This is quite the dangerous object to be handling what with the spikes all around the edges but once it's fastened to your arm, it feels very solid and secure. Maybe there's something to this.

rows.original: "Why are you here, really?" you say. "Unless you expect me to believe a pirate beached her ship by accident." "Well, say, if I was here for a reason, I wouldn't go blabbing about it," Maidensbane says. "Let's just say it's easier for us to be here than anywhere else." You glance up at the ship. You don't think her crew are going to be any more forthcoming than she is. "Mayhap something big is out there," she adds. Metaphorically or literally? It’s hard to tell, and she’s not giving you any clues.

rows.original:
"Got any stories to tell?" you ask.
    
    "Hmm," Maidensbane hums, looking out to sea. "When I was a wee lass, I knew a human boy. We did everything together. Inseparable at the hip, they said. He was my best friend fer years. His parents, though... his parents were shite."
    
    Her gaze grows distant. "Eventually we drifted apart. Happens as ye get older, especially when ye become a teenager and start lookin' fer people. Then I left one day, lookin' to make it on my own."
    
    She turns her head to you and smiles grimly. "The next time I heard of him was twenty years later, when his army burned down the village we'd been born in."
    
    "What? Why?" you say.
    
    She shakes her head. "It was just one of many. He'd become a would-be king, makin' a name fer himself throughout the land. I'm sure he thought nothin' of it. Probably forgot I existed."
    
    You meet her eyes. "Is he still alive?"
    
    Maidensbane looks back out to sea. "No."
    
    You don't inquire further.
rows.translation:
有什么故事想讲吗？”你问道。

“嗯，”少女克星若有所思地望着大海说道，“当我还是个小女孩的时候，认识了一个人类男孩。我们一起做所有的事情，人们都说我们形影不离。他是我多年来最好的朋友。不过他的父母……他的父母真的很糟糕。”

她的目光渐渐变得遥远。“最终，我们渐渐疏远了。随着年龄的增长，这种情况就会发生，尤其是当你进入青少年时期，开始开始关注异性时。后来有一天，我离开了，决定独自生活。她转过头来，对你露出苦涩的笑容：“后来我又听说他的消息，是在二十年后——那时他的军队烧毁了我们出生的那个村庄。”

“什么？为什么？”你问道。

她摇了摇头。那只是众多事件中的一件而已。他原本也想成为国王，在全国各地扬名立万。我敢肯定，他当时根本没把这件事当回事，或许甚至忘记了我的存在。”

你与她对视着。“他现在还活着吗？”

梅登斯贝恩再次望向大海。不。”

你没有再追问下去。

rows.original:
[flags.MAIDENSBANE_TEMP_TAKE
        |You turn.
        
        "Leaving? Good," Maidensbane says, smiling amicably. "Can’t have landlubbers aboard fer too long, s’bad luck."
        
        It's an odd feeling coming aboard a pirate ship – well, a pirate's stolen ship – to take loot and then harmoniously leave, but you've made your peace with it. You slide back down the chain, landing in the depression created by the anchor and climbing free. Maidensbane gives you a wave from atop the ship.
        
        "Be ready for next time!" she calls. "Won't be goin' easy on ye."
        
        So she says.
        |You [party.som
            |turn
            |glance at [party.compNames]
            |glance back at your companions
        ].
        
        "If yer leavin', just know I'll give ye another fight the next time," Maidensbane says. "An' I won't be goin' easy on ye."
        
        So she says. You set back on your journey.
    ]

rows.original:
Traveling along the coast, you can feel the salty sea breeze on your face. The beach is empty save for a lone longship moored in the sand, rugged with brine and cakes of salt covering the bow. [pc.isBimbo
        |This poor ship could totally use some soap. And those striped sails would be really cute if you painted them pink. Oh, oh, and a bunch of sun-tanned sailors with huge cocks!
        |No damage but a lot of dirt; this ship is probably seeing a lot of action by a caring crew. 
    ]
    
    Your thoughts are interrupted by a battlecry that rings out along the beach as a trio of armed warriors jump down from the ship.
    
    [flags.ORC_RAIDERS_ENCOUNTER
        |It looks like those raiding orcs are still plaguing the shores. You duck in the nick of time as Bosht's arrow flies over your head.
        
        "That's right," you hear Amberoga growl. "Hand over your coin or I tell Bosht to aim for your backdoor."
        
        Amberoga underlines her threat by slapping Bosht's ass, making the lizard thrall blush as the Thane fondles her property.
        
        [party.has Arona
            |"These bitches are getting on my nerves," Arona mutters as she readies her weapons. "Wanna teach them who's the top dog, [pc.name]?"
            
            "Of course," you answer and ready your [pc.weapon]. "Why don't you take the lead?"
            
            Your orc companion bellows with laughter as she leads the charge.
            |"You assholes again," you sigh and ready your [pc.weapon]. "I hope your witch knows healing magic."
            
            The trio raises their weapons and you prepare for a fight.
        ]
        |You barely have time to make out who they are before an arrow whips past your cheek.
        
        "Next one will hit," a rumbling voice cries out. "Give us your coin or you'll be leaking from more than one hole."
        
        You squint to get a better look at your assailants. The leader, you assume, is a towering orc woman dressed in a sturdy leather coat with fur lining its collar. You can see her towering mohawk bob in the wind and an eyepatch covering her left eye.
        
        The archer looks like a young, athletic man wearing a simple flax-weaved tunic and pants. He's got scales along his cheeks and neck while his fat crocodilian tail bats the sand.
        
        The third seems to be another voluptuous she-orc just as tall as the leader, even though the leader's mohawk makes her look a couple of inches taller. The thick woman carries a crude staff and wears a long fur cloak that reaches her ankles. It's left open in the middle, revealing her tattooed stomach.
        
        [party.has Arona
            |"Are these yours?" you ask Arona.
            
            "Nah. Never seen them," your brutish follower answers. "Not every tusked bitch you meet is Kervus, you know."
            
            "Just making sure so we're not beating up one of your [arona.isChief
                |underlings
                |kin
            ]," you answer and ready your [pc.weapon].
            
            "That's what I'm talking about!" Arona roars as she charges the raiders together with you.
            |"Are you one of those Kervus types?" you shout at them.
            
            "We are not," the scarred leader answers. "Why would we be part of that loser tribe?"
            
            "Don't worry. The Frost Marches has room for two loser tribes," you shout as you prepare for combat.
        ]
    ]
rows.translation:
沿着海岸线前行，你可以感受到咸咸的海风拂过面庞。海滩上空无一人，只有一艘孤零零的长船停泊在沙滩上，船头被海水侵蚀得粗糙不堪，上面还覆盖着一层盐粒。[pc.isBimbo
        |这艘破旧的船真的需要好好清洗一下了。要是把那些条纹帆涂成粉色，肯定会非常可爱。哦，对了，再配上一群皮肤晒得黝黑、长着巨大鸡巴的水手们，那就更完美了！
        |没有受到任何损坏，但上面积满了灰尘；这艘船肯定是由一群细心负责的船员们精心维护的。 
    ]
    
    你的思绪被一声战斗呐喊打断了——随着三名武装战士从船上跳下来，这声呐喊在海滩上回荡开来。
    
    [flags.ORC_RAIDERS_ENCOUNTER
        |那些劫掠的兽人似乎仍在海岸边肆虐。就在博什特的箭从你头顶飞过的瞬间，你迅速躲了开来。
        
        “没错，”你听到安贝罗加低吼道，“把你的钱交出来，否则我就让博什特瞄准你的后门。”
        
        安贝罗加一边说着，一边拍了拍博什特的屁股，这让这个蜥蜴奴仆的脸颊变得通红——因为这位领主正在抚摸她的财产。
        
        [party.has Arona
            |“这些婊子真让我心烦，”阿罗娜一边准备武器一边嘟囔道，“想让她们知道谁才是真正的老大吗？[pc.name]？”
            
            “当然，”你回答道，同时做好了准备[pc.weapon]。“为什么不让你带头呢？”
            
            你的兽人同伴哈哈大笑着，然后率先冲了上去。
            |“你们这些混蛋又来了，”你叹了口气，然后准备应对他们[pc.weapon]。“希望你的女巫懂得治疗魔法。”
            
            三人举起了武器，你也准备好了迎战。
        ]
        |你还没来得及看清他们是谁，一支箭就已经从你脸颊旁飞过。
        
        “下一支箭就会射中，”一个低沉的声音喊道，“把你的钱交出来，否则你身上就会多出好几个窟窿。”
        
        你眯起眼睛，试图更清楚地看清那些袭击你的人。你猜测，他们的头目是一个高大的兽人女性，她穿着一件结实的皮革外套，衣领处还镶着毛皮。你可以看到她那高高的莫霍克发型在风中飘动，而她的左眼则被眼罩遮住了。
        
        这位弓箭手看起来像是一位年轻、体格健壮的男子，他穿着简单的亚麻布长袍和裤子。他的脸颊和脖子上长满了鳞片，而那条粗壮的鳄鱼尾巴则在沙地上拍打着。
        
        第三位看起来也是一位身材丰满的女性兽人，她的身高与领头者相当——尽管领头者那头莫霍克发型让她看起来似乎高了几英寸。那个身材敦实的女人手持一根粗陋的棍棒，身披一件长及脚踝的毛皮斗篷。斗篷的腰腹处敞开着，露出了她身上纹着的图案。
        
        [party.has Arona
            |“这些是你的吗？”你问阿罗娜。
            
            “不是。我从没见过这些，”你的那个粗野的跟班回答道，“你知道的，并不是每个长着獠牙的女人都叫克沃斯。”
            
            “我只是想确认一下，免得我们打错了人，对自己人动手[arona.isChief
                |手下们
                |亲属
            ]，”你回答道，同时准备好了[pc.weapon]。
            
            “就是这个意思！”阿罗娜一边吼叫，一边与你一起冲向那些袭击者。
            |“你们也是那些克沃斯族的人吗？”你朝他们喊道。
            
            “我们不是，”那个带着伤痕的领头者回答道，“我们为什么要加入那个失败的部落呢？”
            
            “别担心，霜冻边境足够容纳两个失败的部落，”你边说边准备战斗。
        ]
    ]

[flags.ORC_RAIDERS_ENCOUNTER
        |"Fucking shit," Amberoga complains as she falls on her ass. "Ishtun! Where are those fucking thunderbolts? And what is that shit aim, Bosht? Did you get into the ale stash again?"
        
        Both Ishtun and Bosht ignore the Thane's complaining and wait for your move.
        
        "You know the drill," you say. "Get up. And leave those weapons on the ground."
        
        They do as told and Amberoga spits in the sand as she gets to her feet.
        
        "What now, [pc.race]?"
        |The spear-wielding leader growls as she falls under the might of your attacks.
        
        "Shit!" she shouts as she spits in the sand.
        
        "It would seem we've met our match, Roga," the witch calmly hums as she kneels next to the Thane.
        
        "I can fucking see that," the muscled warrior mutters. She looks over at the reptilian archer who's rubbing his bruised chest, then at you with a deep scowl.
        
        "What now, [pc.ra orc
            |mainlander
            |[pc.race]
        ]?" she asks in a defiant voice.
        
        "Get up," you command. "Leave your weapons on the ground. No funny business."
        
        "You heard the [pc.mf
            |man
            |lady
        ]," the curvy witch says and lends a hand to her grumpy comrade. The defeated brute growls and swats away the helping hand as she scrambles to her feet.

“不，不是那种意思。他们看起来没被腐化或怎么样——天知道围城期间我们见过的这类东西已经够一辈子受的了。”她叹了口气，缩回身子，缓缓朝你点了点头。“只是……” 说下去…… “你会看到年轻公牛们在竞技场前、在广场上闲晃，纯粹消磨时间、找乐子。这些家伙鳞片多了点，但身上有同样的气质；至少他们还在用自己的人生做点有用的事，比那些公牛强多了。那些家伙最后通常会变成打零工的，或者混进军团里去，诸如此类。 ”要不是我选择离开、要不是我遇见了你，我很可能也会跟那种人混在一起，而且，嗯——“ 啊。 ”你要是想上去交个朋友，应该没问题。这大概是最好的选择，除非你愿意等上几个小时等他们干完；我这辈子也处理宰杀过一两次那么大的东西。“ |”他们看起来玩得很开心。“清子从你肩后低声说道。她没有像你那样探头张望——这种事对像她这样的人来说大概太失体面了——只是静静观察，相信自己的天性足以不被人察觉。”也许您该上前自我介绍一下，挚爱。外交之类的事。“ 她说，外交。 ”他们也是人，不是吗？只是享受着存在，并以自己工作的成功为傲。“你的狐狸[kiyoko.married |妻子 |情人 ]迟疑了片刻。”我感觉不到他们之中有谁心怀恶意，所以就算出了什么问题，也尽可以算在您头上。当然，我对您的能力有绝对的信心，挚爱。“ 你感觉自己在被人推着往某件事里走…… ”如果您是这个意思，我并不打算在这里干等上几个小时等他们完工。来吧，我心爱的人总不至于怕生吧？“ |一看清你在做什么，阿兹兰便抢先上前一步，一边打量着那场面，一边轻轻把你往后推。这份无私令人感激，可她全身披着甲壳、手里还握着[azyrran.weapon]，实在算不上不起眼。你不太确定她为什么突然这么做，但过了好一会儿，阿兹兰终于转过身来，朝你露出一个小小的微笑。 ”好吧，虚惊一场。我还以为他们可能……嗯。我们见过的当地人里，没几个能毫发无伤地躲过恶魔的推进，对吧？“ 而这些佩克西加斯特就躲过了？ ”乍看之下，我觉得是。我和姐妹们去袭击那些傻乎乎的小蜜蜂、给她们找点乐子之后，大概也是这副样子——没什么不寻常的。没有犄角，身上也没溅满精液，看起来也不像是急着要打架；只要咱们好好自我介绍，我想可以跟他们谈谈。在这片灰暗的惨景里能看到一张友善的脸，真好。那咱们就上去打个招呼？“ |”怎么了？“阿罗娜从后面撞上你时咕哝道。”你不会是怕了他们这几个吧？他们又没那么能打；不然我们也留不住帕沃。“ 你不是害怕，只是想保存体力。恶魔也许已经从科尔米诺斯撤退了，但海岸地带远谈不上安全，你不想把精力浪费在无谓的打斗上。 她咧嘴一笑。”不懂你什么意思。要真想把自己累趴下，没什么比好好打一场更痛快的了。“ 她完全明白你在说什么；阿罗娜早已不是当年那个满山麓乱跑找麻烦的兽人了。 ”是啊，可我们现在就在这些悬崖上到处乱爬，浑身痒痒地想搞点乱子。我看不出有什么不一样，不过随你便。“ |你正要再靠近些、把这伙人看得更清楚，却发现昆因已经在办了——他爬上了一处低矮的岩架，那里能更好地观察这群人。你决定把这事交给受过专业训练的人，于是退回去等昆因回来汇报。他果然照做了，跳回灰色的沙地上，朝你点了点头、竖起大拇指。 那你是说这些佩克西加斯特没有威胁？ ”我暂时还不会那么肯定。“他咧嘴一笑。”但很明显他们没跟托勒斯、恶魔或者那种东西混在一起。我看得出来。依我看，不过是一群出来找点乐子的家伙，可是……小心一点总没坏处，以防万一。感觉他们是那种如果你不小心侮辱了他们老妈，就会立刻暴怒的年轻小公牛。“ 你并不打算说错话。 ”你在考虑上去打个招呼？“ 谁知道他们要处理那具尸体多久，如果他们可以接近，你也不觉得有什么坏处。他们也许能告诉你一些关于海岸地带现况的事。 ”嗯。随你便。“ |”有意思。“薇薇安挠着下巴若有所思地说。”他们似乎没被当地的制御触碰过。我真希望能上去仔细看看他们，[pc.name]。说真的，佩克西加斯特是个独特得迷人的族群。“ 那她估计这里安全吗？ 她笑了一声。”我可没说过那种话——他们没有被[viviane.isDemon |触碰 |侵蚀 ]，并不意味着他们会张开双臂欢迎我们。但我没有那种感觉，觉得他们会转眼就变成凶残的怪物，一心想要扑上来强暴我们。我只想知道他们是否不知怎么地至今抵抗住了那种制御，还是只是刚来这片地方、还没碰上机会。“ 好吧，既然她这么有把握，你也不觉得满足一下她的好奇心有什么坏处。那就去吧？ |”怎么了？我们为什么停下——“你感到肩上一沉，阿格妮和你一起从悬崖后面探出头来。”哦。“ 你们俩又盯着那些佩克西加斯特看了好一会儿，然后退回到石头后面。她觉得那伙人怎么样？ ”他们没被腐化，至少外表上没有。这有点奇怪，因为我们一路下来遇到的东西大多都变成了某种程度的发情操兽。另一方面，他们显然是从海里出来的，所以也许只是因为他们不是这地方的人。“ 你同意阿格妮的看法——在一条不久前还爬满恶魔的海岸线上，这些佩克西加斯特正常得令人吃惊。那么，也许你该上去打个招呼？说不定他们对这一带发生的事能说上几句。 她谨慎地点了点头。”他们感觉……说实话，就像我演出过的多数观众。只是一群出来找乐子的家伙。我不会说他们无害——天知道我这几辈子见过多少场架打起来——但他们看起来人还不错。那就去吧？“ |你正要再靠近些、把这伙人看得更清楚，却瞥见哈里克正在狩猎队上方的空中盘旋。你意识到小琳已经在办了，而且大概比你待在这里能查到的结果更好，于是悄悄退回悬崖的掩蔽处，等哈里克回到它的女主人身边。几分钟后，哈里克侦察完毕，落回小琳的手臂上，你这才走上前，朝后者点了点头。 哈里克看到什么有趣的东西了吗？ ”关于那些佩克西加斯特？就他所能判断的，他们只是普通人。“ 而这本身就很有意思——恶魔穿过海岸地带、一路推进到科尔米诺斯东门的行军，在这片土地和居民身上都留下了痕迹。如果他们被腐化触碰过，也许只是还没在外表上显现出来。 小琳一边挠着哈里克一边思考着这件事。”我不觉得是那样。当初……当初宫里情况变糟的时候，哈里克仍然能感觉到哪些人被腐化了，哪怕他们外表看着没问题。他觉得这些家伙有点闹腾，但完全不是那种人。我觉得我们可以跟他们谈谈，[pc.name]。“ 确实。在这个时间、这个地点，正常本身就能让这支狩猎队显得特别，这也说明了些什么，不过也许这些佩克西加斯特能告诉你更多。 |你又观察了那支狩猎队好一会儿，他们的行为似乎没什么不寻常——可稍微一想，正是这一点让人觉得古怪。恶魔穿过海岸地带、一路推进到科尔米诺斯东门的行军，在这片土地和居民身上都留下了痕迹。佩克西加斯特身上的腐化也许只是还没在外表上显现出来，可是……不，这跟你所见到的也对不上。没错，他们很闹腾，但更像是一群出来找乐子的家伙，仅此而已——身为狩猎队，他们当然算不上无害，但他们也并非充满敌意。 那么大一具尸体，天知道他们要处理到什么时候，而且这片海滩也没别的路可绕。也许他们能告诉你一些海岸地带近来发生的事？ 带着这个念头，你决定碰碰运气，从悬崖后走了出来。 ]
rows.raw: " Making your way down the gray, pebbly beach, you pause as a commotion up ahead breaks up the dreary monotony of the coastlands. Rapacious hooting and cheering rises from around one of the limestone cliffs, an absolute hullabaloo of excitement that makes no effort to disguise itself. With the beach being one long narrow strip at the foot of the cliffs, whoever's making the ruckus is directly in your path, and it feels prudent to edge closer and peek around the nearest cliff face. As it turns out, the source of all this noise is a hunting party of a half-dozen pexighasts — lizard-folk — who've brought down a large walrus on the beach and are just getting to dressing the fresh carcass. Each and every one of them happens to be a big, burly male to some degree — one wonders if there's any cultural significance to that — and they're completely naked save for the occasional skin-tight kelp wrap to obscure their reptilian genital slits. With their painted bodies still wet with moisture, it's clear that this hunting party emerged from the waves, and intend to take their haul back with them; the pexighasts chatter excitedly amongst themselves in a vaguely sibilant tongue as they take turns cutting their prize down into more manageable parts, congratulating each other on a job well done with playful punches and jabs. [party.randComp cait brint brienne kiyoko azyrran arona quintillus vivianne agni ryn |"For once, someone's actually smiling!" Cait says as she peeks around the cliff with you. "These must be pretty great guys if they're able to have fun here, of all places!" You catch your pink kitten's eye, and she gives you a wink. Sure, that was a bit of hyperbole on Cait's part, but... the coastlands are pretty dreary. Still, do these guys pass her smell test? "I don't think they're with the demons, tainted or anything like that, if that's what you're asking; they feel like just a bunch of guys looking for any kind of fun they can get their hands on. We'd get a bunch of these sorts at the temple every so often, anubians rich with spice money looking for the passions we had on offer. I wouldn't be against it if you wanted to go up and say hi!" |Brint chuckles as he peeks around the cliff with you, an impressive maneuver considering his size. "Oh." Oh? "These lots. You see bulls hanging around the colosseum every day killing time, looking for fun — good chance I'd have fallen in with one of those types if I hadn't left home and met you." He gives you a wink and nod. "These ones may be a bit scalier, but I daresay they're just as harmless. If anything, they're doing something useful, which is more than I can say for my own." Does he reckon they're safe to approach, then? "They don't look like they've been tainted or anything — gods know we've seen enough of those for a lifetime during the siege. Should be good, so long as we keep our heads on our shoulders." |Brienne hums as she peeks around the cliff with you, quite the impressive maneuver considering the size of the heifer she is. "O-oh." Something wrong? She seems a little off-put by the band, should you prepare for trouble? "No, not like that. They don't look like they've been tainted or anything — gods know we've seen enough of those kinds for a lifetime during the siege." She sighs, pulls herself back, and gives you a slow nod. "It's just that..." Go on... "You see young bulls hanging out in front of the colosseum, in the fora, just killing time and looking for fun. These guys are scalier, but they've got the same energy about them; at least they're doing something useful with their lives, which is more than I can say for those bulls. They usually end up as day laborers, drift into the legion, that kind of thing. "There's a good chance I might've fallen in with one of those kinds if I hadn't chosen to leave, if I hadn't met you, and, well —" Ah. "It should be fine if you want to go up and make friends. Probably the best choice, unless you want to wait hours for them to be done; I've dressed and butchered a thing or two that size in my time." |"They look like they are having fun," Kiyoko murmurs from around your shoulder. She isn't peering like you are — probably too undignified for the likes of her — but simply observes, trusting in her nature to remain unnoticed. "Perhaps you should go up and introduce yourself, Beloved. Diplomacy and all." Diplomacy, she says. "They are people, are they not? Simply enjoying existence and taking pride in the success of one's work." Your fox-[kiyoko.married |wife |lover ] demurs a moment. "I sense no malice in any of them, so any problems that arise can be safely laid at your feet. Of course, I have utmost confidence in your abilities, Beloved." You get the feeling that you're being pushed into something here... "I do not intend to wait around here for hours until they finish their task, if that is your meaning. Come on, surely my beloved is not shy to meet new people?" |Once she sees what you're about, Azyrran takes point and steps forward, eyeing the scene while gently nudging you to step back. The selflessness is appreciated, but she isn't the most inconspicuous all clad in chitin and with her [azyrran.weapon] out. You're not sure what exactly prompted this from her, but at length Azyrran turns back to you with a small smile. "Okay, false alarm. I thought they might've been... well. Not many of the locals we've seen have escaped the demon advance unscathed, have they?" And these pexighasts aren't? "Not at a glance, I don't think. My sisters and I would be much the same after raiding those silly little bees and showing them a good time — nothing out of the ordinary. No horns, no cum splattered all over them, and they don't look like they're itching for a fight; I think we can talk to them so long as we introduce ourselves properly. It's nice to be able to see a friendly face in all this gray misery. Shall we go up and say hi, then?" |"What's the matter?" Arona grunts as she bumps into you from behind. "You're not afraid of a handful of their like, are you? It's not like they're very tough or anything; we wouldn't have been able to keep Pavo otherwise." You're not afraid, but you want to pace yourself. The demons may have retreated from Khor'Minos, but the coastlands are far from safe, you don't want to waste your energy getting into needless fights. A grin. "Don't know what you mean. If I'm going to tire myself out, no better way to do it than a good tussle." She knows full well what you're getting at; Arona's hardly the orc she once was, traipsing all over the foothills looking for trouble. "No, but we're crawling all over these cliffs and itching for some shenanigans. Doesn't seem that different to me, but suit yourself." |You're about to edge closer and get a better handle on the group when you realize Quin's already on the task, having clambered up on a low ledge that offers a better view of the group. Deciding to leave the matter someone who's been trained in the matter, you withdraw and wait for Quin to return and report. He does just that, hopping back down onto the gray sands and giving you a nod and thumbs-up. You take the pexighasts aren't any threat, then? "I wouldn't go that far just yet." He grins. "But it's clear they're not with Tollus, demons, or anything of that kind. I'd know. Just a bunch of guys out and about looking for a bit of fun, that's my measure, but... it always pays to be a little careful, just in case. Feel like the type of young bucks to get real mad in a hurry if you accidentally insult their mom, that kind of thing." You weren't intending to put your foot in your mouth. "You thinking of going up and saying hello?" Who knows how long they'll be dressing that carcass, and if they're approachable then you don't see the harm in it. They might be able to tell you something about the state of the coastlands. "Hm. Suit yourself." |"Interesting," Vivane muses, scratching her chin. "They don't seem to have been touched by the local influences. I'd love if we could go up and get a closer look at them, [pc.name]. Pexighasts are a uniquely fascinating people, when you get down to it." She reckons it's safe, then? A laugh. "I didn't say anything of that sort — just because they haven't been [viviane.isDemon |touched |afflicted ] doesn't mean they'll welcome us with open arms. But I don't get the feeling that the lot of them will turn into vicious monsters intent on forcing themselves upon us at the drop of a hat. I just want to know if they've somehow been able to resist the influence thus far, or if they're merely new to the area and haven't had the chance yet." Well, if she's that confident, you don't see any harm in indulging her curiosity. Shall you, then? |"What's the matter? Why've we stopp —" You feel a weight on your shoulder as Agni peers around the cliff with you. "Oh." The both of you eye the pexighasts for a few more moments, then retreat back around the stone. What does she think of that lot? "They aren't tainted, at least not on the outside. Which is a little odd, because most everything we've met on our descent has been turned into some degree of horny fuck-beast. On the other hand, they did obviously come out of the sea, so maybe it's just that they aren't around from here." You agree with Agni's sentiments — the pexighasts look shockingly normal for a strip of coastline that was recently crawling with demons. Well, perhaps you should go up and say hello? Maybe they'll have something to say about what's been happening around these parts. A cautious nod. "They feel like... like most audiences I've played for, honestly. Just a bunch of guys out for a bit of fun. I wouldn't call them harmless — gods know I've seen enough brawls break out in all my lives — but they seem like decent enough people. Shall we, then?" |You're about to edge closer and get a better handle on the group when you spy Harrick wheeling in the air above the hunting party. Realizing Ryn's already on the job and probably getting better results than you can from where you are, you slink back into the cover of the cliffs and wait for Harrick to return to his mistress. It's a handful of minutes before he finishes scouting and returns to Ryn's arm, whereupon you step up and give the latter a nod. Did Harrick see anything interesting? "About the pexighasts? They're just normal people, as far as he can tell." Which is interesting in and of itself — the demons' march up through the coastlands to the eastern gates of Khor'minos has left its mark on the landscape and inhabitants. If they've been touched by the corruption, maybe it just hasn't manifested outwardly. Ryn thinks about that while she scritches Harrick. "I don't think that's the case. Back when... when things were getting bad in the palace, Harrick still had a sense for people who'd been tainted, even if they were outwardly fine. He thinks these guys are a bit rowdy, but aren't like that at all. I think we can talk to them, [pc.name]." Indeed. It says something that being normal in this time and place is what makes this hunting party stand out, but maybe the pexighasts can tell you more. |You watch the hunting party for several more moments, but their behavior doesn't seem out of the ordinary — which, after a little thought, is exactly what makes it odd. The demons' march up through the coastlands to the eastern gates of Khor'minos has left its mark on the landscape and inhabitants. It's possible that any possible taint the pexighasts might have just hasn't manifested outwardly, but... no, that doesn't match up with what you're seeing, either. Sure, they're rowdy, but it's more in the fashion of a bunch of guys out looking to have a good time than anything — being a hunting party means they're certainly not harmless, but they're not hostile, either. With a carcass that size, the gods know how long it'll be before they're done with it, and there's no way around this stretch of beach, either. Maybe they can tell you something about what's been happening in the coastlands? With that thought in mind, you decide to take your chances and step out from the cliffs. ] "

rows.original: You aren't trying to hide yourself, and the pexighasts spot you easily as you stride forward over the coarse, pebbly beach. Once they note your open stance and empty hands, though, they relax their grip on their bone spears and settle down, although it's clear that they're still on guard. After a brief discussion in their own language, one of the pexighasts detaches from the group and steps forward, speaking in broken Belharan; with how he breaks up and stumbles over the syllables, it's clear that his voice is better suited for speaking underwater than on land. [party.oneComp brint brienne |"Ho, a bull from the city above! You're a sight for sore eyes — does that mean the legions are coming?" "Not this far down, and not just yet," Brint replies. "They're mostly busy with picking up the pieces after the siege. It'll be a while before someone starts thinking about taking the fight to Khor'Elthos, I'm afraid." "Ah, not the best news, but at least it's good to hear the city's still safe and standing. You didn't look much like a legionnaire, anyways." Brint grins. "We're scouts of a sort, I guess." |"Ho, a lady bull from the city above! You're a sight for sore eyes — does that mean people are coming down to fix everything that's broken?" "Not every cowgirl's an architect or engineer, you know. Would that I were elevated as high as one of the city mothers." Brienne sighs, perhaps a little too wistfully. "But no. There's a lot that needs fixing in the wake of the siege — I'm afraid it'll be a while before anyone concerns themselves with what lies beyond the gates." "Shame, but we weren't hoping for anyone to come save us or anything." The pexighast does a little show of flexing his muscles, much to the snickering of his fellows. "Still, it's good to hear the city's safe. You didn't much look like builders, anyway." Brienne lowers her eyes, shuffling closer to you. "We're... scouts, I guess that'd be the best way of putting it." |"Ho there, [pc.race]! You can speak, can't you?" Yes, you can. Have things gotten so bad that even that's called into question? "Well, I guess it's less 'can' and more 'want to' — most people my band's run into weren't the friendliest. You're from the bull-city up top? The air of the place's clinging thickly on you." You came down the cliffs from Khor'minos, if that's what's he's asking. A nod. "Any hope the legions are going to be coming down anytime soon?" Afraid not. There're still very many pieces left to pick up from the siege before Khor'minos can think about sending feelers out beyond the mountain. "A siege, huh? Oh, well. Not that we were hoping for someone to save us or anything." ] So, you've introduced yourselves — what's their deal, then? You're guessing they're locals, right? The pexighast scratches his head. "I guess you could call us that. We don't live here here — more under the ocean, if anything — but yes, we knew the bull people in the city by the bay and a few more by the beach. Until they all left, that is." Right, everyone living in the coastlands was evacuated and took refuge in Khor'minos. "Yeah. Figured that we didn't want any part of the trouble that was brewing, so we took that same advice and decided to stay home for a bit, keep our heads under the waves. But now that things have settled down a little, a bunch of us lads got itchy fins and thought we'd head back to see what's going on, maybe bring a little something to take home while at it. We haven't been bothered that much, and most trouble isn't willing to follow us into the water. "Look, we saw you coming down the cliffs, beat down a few troublemakers that might've come over and bothered us — the road from the mountain to the beach isn't exactly hidden, and noise carries. Whether you meant it or not, the lads and I owe you one, which is why we're standing here talking. Having the likes of you hanging around means the beach's just that much safer for us, so you're welcome to what hospitality we have." Sounds good. Were there any questions you wanted to ask the pexighasts, or are you ready to move on?
rows.translation: 你并没有刻意隐藏自己，当你大步走过粗糙的卵石海滩时，佩克西加斯特们轻易就发现了你。不过，一看到你姿态坦荡、两手空空，他们便放松了握骨矛的手，安静下来，虽然很明显他们仍保持警惕。用他们自己的语言简短商议一番之后，一只佩克西加斯特脱离队伍走上前来，用生硬的贝尔哈兰语开口；从他断句和音节上的磕绊来看，他的嗓子显然更适合在水下说话，而不是在陆地上。 [party.oneComp brint brienne |“嚯，一位来自上方城市的公牛！见到你真是让人眼睛一亮——这是说军团要来了吗？” “还下不到这么远，也不是现在，”布林特回答。“他们大多在忙着收拾围城后的烂摊子。恐怕还得过上一阵子，才会有人开始考虑主动出击科尔埃尔斯奥斯。” “啊，这消息不算好，但至少听说城里还安全、还立着，这就让人高兴了。反正你看起来也不太像军团士兵。” 布林特咧嘴一笑。“算是侦察兵之类的吧。” |“嚯，一位来自上方城市的母牛！见到你真是让人眼睛一亮——这是说有人要下来修好所有坏掉的东西了吗？” “你知道，不是每个牛姑娘都是建筑师或工程师。我倒希望自己能像城里的母亲们那样地位尊崇。”布蕾妮叹了口气，也许叹得有点太惆怅了。“但不行。围城之后有太多东西要修——恐怕还得过上一阵子，才会有人去操心城门之外的事。” “可惜，不过我们也没指望有人来救我们什么的。”那只佩克西加斯特小小地展示了一下自己鼓起的肌肉，惹得同伴们窃笑。“不过，听说城里安全还是挺好的。反正你看起来也不怎么像建筑工。” 布蕾妮垂下眼睛，往你身边挪了挪。“我们……算是侦察兵吧，我觉得这是最合适的说法。” |“嚯，那边的[pc.race]！你会说话，对吧？” 是的，你会说话。情况已经糟到连这种事都要被质疑了吗？ “嗯，我想与其说是‘会不会’，不如说是‘想不想’——我这队人碰到的多数人都不怎么友善。你是从上面那座公牛城来的？那地方的气息还厚厚地黏在你身上。” 如果他是这个意思的话，你是从科尔米诺斯沿着悬崖下来的。 他点了点头。“军团有希望很快下来吗？” 恐怕没有。科尔米诺斯要考虑往山外派出触角之前，围城留下的烂摊子还有太多太多要收拾。 “围城，是吧？哦，好吧。我们倒也不是指望有人来救我们什么的。” ] 那么，你们已经互相介绍过了——他们到底是什么来头？你猜他们是当地人，对吧？ 那只佩克西加斯特挠了挠头。“我猜你可以这么叫我们。我们并不住在这里的这里——要说的话更像住在海底下——不过没错，我们认识海湾城里那些牛头人，也认识海滩边的一些。直到他们全都离开了，就是这样。” 对了，住在海岸地带的居民全都被疏散了，到科尔米诺斯避难去了。 “是啊。我们想着不想掺和正在酝酿的麻烦，于是也听了同样的劝告，决定先在家里待一阵子，把脑袋埋在水波下面。可现在事情稍微平息了些，我们这帮兄弟就鳍痒难耐，想着回来看看情况，顺便带点东西回家。我们没受到多少骚扰，而大多数麻烦也不愿意跟着我们进水。 ”你看，我们看到你从悬崖上下来，打退了一些本可能过来骚扰我们的捣乱分子——从山到海滩的路又不是藏起来的，动静也会传出去。不管你有没有这个意思，我和兄弟们欠你一份情，所以我们才会站在这儿跟你说话。有你这样的人在附近晃荡，海滩对我们来说就安全多了，所以我们有什么招待，你尽管享用。“ 听起来不错。你有什么问题想问这些佩克西加斯特，还是准备继续上路了？
rows.raw: " You aren't trying to hide yourself, and the pexighasts spot you easily as you stride forward over the coarse, pebbly beach. Once they note your open stance and empty hands, though, they relax their grip on their bone spears and settle down, although it's clear that they're still on guard. After a brief discussion in their own language, one of the pexighasts detaches from the group and steps forward, speaking in broken Belharan; with how he breaks up and stumbles over the syllables, it's clear that his voice is better suited for speaking underwater than on land. [party.oneComp brint brienne |"Ho, a bull from the city above! You're a sight for sore eyes — does that mean the legions are coming?" "Not this far down, and not just yet," Brint replies. "They're mostly busy with picking up the pieces after the siege. It'll be a while before someone starts thinking about taking the fight to Khor'Elthos, I'm afraid." "Ah, not the best news, but at least it's good to hear the city's still safe and standing. You didn't look much like a legionnaire, anyways." Brint grins. "We're scouts of a sort, I guess." |"Ho, a lady bull from the city above! You're a sight for sore eyes — does that mean people are coming down to fix everything that's broken?" "Not every cowgirl's an architect or engineer, you know. Would that I were elevated as high as one of the city mothers." Brienne sighs, perhaps a little too wistfully. "But no. There's a lot that needs fixing in the wake of the siege — I'm afraid it'll be a while before anyone concerns themselves with what lies beyond the gates." "Shame, but we weren't hoping for anyone to come save us or anything." The pexighast does a little show of flexing his muscles, much to the snickering of his fellows. "Still, it's good to hear the city's safe. You didn't much look like builders, anyway." Brienne lowers her eyes, shuffling closer to you. "We're... scouts, I guess that'd be the best way of putting it." |"Ho there, [pc.race]! You can speak, can't you?" Yes, you can. Have things gotten so bad that even that's called into question? "Well, I guess it's less 'can' and more 'want to' — most people my band's run into weren't the friendliest. You're from the bull-city up top? The air of the place's clinging thickly on you." You came down the cliffs from Khor'minos, if that's what's he's asking. A nod. "Any hope the legions are going to be coming down anytime soon?" Afraid not. There're still very many pieces left to pick up from the siege before Khor'minos can think about sending feelers out beyond the mountain. "A siege, huh? Oh, well. Until they all left, that is." Right, everyone living in the coastlands was evacuated and took refuge in Khor'minos. "Yeah. Figured that we didn't want any part of the trouble that was brewing, so we took that same advice and decided to stay home for a bit, keep our heads under the waves. But now that things have settled down a little, a bunch of us lads got itchy fins and thought we'd head back to see what's going on, maybe bring a little something to take home while at it. Whether you meant it or not, the lads and I owe you one, which is why we're standing here talking. Having the likes of you hanging around means the beach's just that much safer for us, so you're welcome to what hospitality we have." Sounds good. Were there any questions you wanted to ask the pexighasts, or are you ready to move on? "

rows.original: They sure made a mess of the coastlands, didn't they?
rows.translation: 他们可真是把海岸地带搞得一团糟，不是吗？
rows.raw: "They sure made a mess of the coastlands, didn't they?"

rows.original: Did they traffic a lot with the people of Khor'Elthos? What's become of the city now?
rows.translation: 他们以前常和科尔埃尔斯奥斯的人往来吗？那座城现在怎么样了？
rows.raw: "Did they traffic a lot with the people of Khor'Elthos? What's become of the city now?"

rows.original: What's with the locals, anyway? Any reason they're so ornery all of a sudden?
rows.translation: 那这些当地人到底怎么回事？他们怎么突然变得这么暴躁？
rows.raw: "What's with the locals, anyway? Any reason they're so ornery all of a sudden?"

rows.original: "It's a lot colder without all the people around, and I don't just mean like ice. Like it or not, there used to be people coming and going between the waterfront and the mountain, and now it's all empty, like an oyster without the meat in it. The sky and cliffs seem so much more grey than what it was like before." He mentioned people being evacuated from the coastlands, presumably ahead of the demons' advance. Did he see any of that? "Nah, even us lads were smart enough to stay home and out of whatever was happening. Even under the water, we could see the demons' boats going down the shoreline, could feel really bad stuff all over the cliffs. Curiosity just wasn't worth it. "That feeling stuck for a good long while until pretty recently, when they started retreating back to the bay, the city they'd taken. Had much less of a menacing air to them, then." Makes sense — that would be about the point when the siege broke. And then the pexighasts felt it was safe enough to come take a look-see at what had happened. "Most of them are still holed up in the bay city; a few leave every so often on so-called patrols that don't accomplish very much. We hear them coming miles away with all the noise they make, so they're pretty easy to avoid. But if you want to pick a fight with any demons you bump into... well, it'd make life easier for us."
rows.translation: “周围的人一走，这里就冷清多了，我说的可不只是像冰那样冷。不管你喜欢不喜欢，以前从水边到山脚下总是人来人往，现在却全空了，就像一只没有肉的牡蛎。天空和悬崖看起来也比以前灰暗得多。” 他提到过海岸地带的居民被疏散了，大概是在恶魔推进之前。他有没有亲眼见到那件事？ “没有，就算是我们这帮兄弟也够聪明，老老实实待在家里，不掺和正在发生的那些事。就算在水下，我们也能看到恶魔的船沿着海岸线驶过，能感觉到悬崖上到处弥漫着非常糟糕的东西。好奇心实在不值得。 ”那种感觉持续了很长一段时间，直到最近他们开始撤回到海湾，也就是他们占领的那座城。那时候他们身上的威胁气息就少多了。“ 说得通——那大概正是围城被打破的时候。然后佩克西加斯特们才觉得足够安全，可以过来看看发生了什么。 ”他们大多数人还窝在海湾那座城里；偶尔有几个会出来搞所谓的巡逻，其实没什么成果。他们弄出的动静那么大，我们在几里之外就听得见，所以要避开很容易。不过你要是想跟碰上的恶魔打一架……嗯，那会让我们的日子好过些。“

rows.original:
The pexighast grins at that and jabs a clawed thumb over a scaly shoulder at his fellows still dressing the carcass. "You can see for yourself, can't you? One of the few good things to come out of all of this."
    
    He's quite pleased with the outcome — and %"come out of all of this"? Did the hunting here change?
    
    "Sure it did. Fat bastard over there's bigger than any walrus we've ever seen along this coastline, he'll feed everyone back home for a good while. He's not the only overgrown thing we've seen these last several days, either — everything from crabs to eels have absolutely chonked out while we were gone. We even spotted a giant sea snail that came up all the way to our knees, those things are usually tiny. Can't eat those, though, poisonous little vermin."
    
    And just to be clear, the local wildlife never used to get that big?
    
    A nod. "I don't know whether it was something the demons did or if everyone moving out from the coast meant critters of this size could come in, but it's what it is. First few kills we made, we took them apart carefully and checked the meat and organs for taint, but we didn't find any diseased growths or anything like in the old stories. The meat's as sweet as it ought to be, I've tried it myself; it just got... uh, larger than it ought to be. Good problem to have, if you ask me.
    
    "I don't know, maybe now that we're here the big ones will eventually go back into hiding after we hunt them a bit. But while they're here, there's no reason to bring a few home for good eating, right?"
rows.translation:
那只佩克西加斯特咧嘴一笑，用带爪的拇指越过布满鳞片的肩膀，指了指还在处理尸体的同伴。“你自己看得到的，对吧？这算是这一切带来的少数好事之一。”
    
    他对这个结果相当满意——而且%“这一切带来的”？这里的狩猎变了吗？
    
    “当然变了。那边那胖混蛋比我们在这条海岸线上见过的任何海象都大，够老家所有人吃上好一阵子。他也不是这几天我们见过的唯一长过头的东西——从螃蟹到鳗鱼，在我们离开的这段时间里全都肥得离谱。我们甚至看到一只巨大的海螺，都长到我们膝盖那么高了，那些东西平时可是很小的。不过那些不能吃，有毒的小害虫。”
    
    再确认一下，本地的野生动物以前从来不会长那么大？
    
    他点了点头。“我不知道那是恶魔搞的鬼，还是因为沿海的人都搬走了，这种体型的生物才敢进来，但事实就是这样。我们头几次猎杀时，都小心地拆开它们，检查肉和内脏有没有腐化，但没发现任何像老故事里那样的病变增生。肉该多鲜甜就多鲜甜，我自己尝过；它只是变……呃，变得比它该有的样子更大了。要我说，这可是好事。
    
    ”我不知道，也许等我们在这儿待久了，把这些大家伙猎上一阵，它们终究又会躲起来。但它们还在这儿的时候，没理由不带几只回家好好吃一顿，对吧？“

rows.original:
"Yeah, we knew them and they knew us. Not like, the city chieftain or anything, but there were bulls living outside of the city walls in the bay who'd do business with us. Sometimes they'd take stuff like deep-sea fish and a few shinies in trade, but our main business was in information."
    
    Information?
    
    "Yeah, on shipwrecks. Even with the lighthouse, the rocks they call the dragon's teeth used to take all kinds of ships trying to approach the coast and bay. Merchants, raiders, everyone in between — me and the other lads, we'd scout out where they'd gone down, tie buoys to mark the place, then tell the bulls in the bay. They'd go out and dredge up anything of value, then pay us well for the find. We'd then go to the docks and spend everything in one place; most bull things don't keep well in water.
    
    "It was a good deal for both of us, bulls by and large are honest people who keep their word. It's a shame what happened to the city."
    
    Yeah, speaking of that... do they know what Khor'Elthos is like now?
    
    "It's still pretty bad — what's left of the demons after they failed to get into the mountain retreated past the bay to lick their wounds. They've been taking the ships the bulls left in the evacuation and sending them out over the water, but it doesn't look like they're running."
    
    Getting reinforcements from somewhere else, maybe?
    
    A shrug. "Could be. There's enough of them in the city that none of us dared to get any closer than the edges of the bay. You heading in that direction, then?"
    
    Now that the siege is over, the minotaurs will probably want to retake the coastlands eventually, if only to not have a demon-occupied city as neighbors. But that's probably a ways off; you're just an advance team.
    
    "Be careful, then. They may be the leftovers, but there're still enough demons that the city's still crawling with them."
rows.translation:
“是啊，我们认识他们，他们也认识我们。不是说城里的酋长那种，但海湾城墙外住着一些牛头人，会跟我们做生意。有时候他们会用深海鱼和几件亮晶晶的小玩意来换东西，但我们主要的生意是情报。”
    
    情报？
    
    “是啊，关于沉船。就算有灯塔，那些被叫做龙牙的礁石也照样吞掉各种想靠近海岸和海湾的船。商人、劫掠者，还有介于两者之间的各色人等——我和其他兄弟会先去查清它们沉在哪里，系上浮标标记位置，然后告诉海湾里的牛头人。他们会出海把值钱的东西都捞上来，然后为这次发现付我们不错的报酬。之后我们就去码头上，把钱在一个地方花个精光；牛头人的东西大多在水里放不久。
    
    ”这对双方都是笔好买卖，牛头人总的来说是讲信用的诚实人。那座城出了这种事，真是可惜。“
    
    是啊，说到这个……他们知道科尔埃尔斯奥斯现在是什么样子吗？
    
    ”还是相当糟——恶魔没能攻进山里之后，剩下的残部退过海湾去舔伤口。他们一直用牛头人在疏散时留下的船，把船派到水面上，但看起来不像是在逃跑。“
    
    也许是从别处调援军？
    
    他耸了耸肩。”有可能。城里他们的数量够多，我们谁也不敢靠近到比海湾边缘更近的地方。那你是要往那个方向去？“
    
    既然围城已经结束，弥诺陶洛斯们大概终究会想夺回海岸地带，哪怕只是为了不让一座被恶魔占领的城当自己的邻居。但那大概还早得很；你只是一支先遣队。
    
    ”那你们小心点。他们也许是残兵剩将，但恶魔还是多得足以让那座城爬满他们。“

rows.original: A short, raspy laugh. "I'm not sure I'd call them 'locals'. Most people we lads bumped into weren't even here before all this started, this coast was mostly bulls and the people who lived in the same hole — hobgoblins, 'manders, those kinds. But since the bulls left and the demons ran back to their city, there's been a whole lot of nothing waiting to be filled." Nature abhors a vacuum? The pexighast creases his brows over the words, then shrugs. "Dunno. Maybe. Just saying there's a lot of space for people to come in, I guess. And how so — just the other day we lads almost bumped face-first into a band of orcs going through the abandoned bull villas and looting everything in sight. I mean, sure we can fight, but we're just hunters. Those gray-skins definitely weren't from around these parts, the orcs who used to come and raid in the past were mostly green-skins. "Honestly, without the bulls keeping order, it's kind of a free-for-all at this point. But since you came all the way down from the mountain, that shouldn't be a surprise to you, yeah?" Are there any locals still hanging around the coastlands? From before, that is, not just people running in to capitalize on the general lawlessness? "Some of the harpies, I guess, although they're not quite right in the head now." The pexighast points up at the sea cliffs. "Couple of us were thinking of having gull eggs and were just about to start the climb when the harpies looked fit to swarm us. Suddenly, we weren't that peckish any more. "They've always been a bit sour-like what with living in their cliffside holes, but now they're five, ten times that. Don't know what happened to them, don't care to find out; so long as we keep to the beach, they don't bother us. But you — I guess it's your job to figure out these things, or else you wouldn't be asking these questions, right? Maybe if you can knock some sense into them, the harpies can tell you more than we can."
rows.translation: 一声短促沙哑的笑。“我不确定我会叫他们‘当地人’。我们这帮兄弟碰到的多数人，在这档子事开始之前根本都不在这儿；这片海岸以前主要是牛头人，还有跟他们住在同一个洞里的那些——大地精、蝾螈人，那一类。可自从牛头人离开、恶魔跑回他们那座城之后，就只剩下大片大片的空缺等着被填上。” 自然厌恶真空？ 那只佩克西加斯特对着这句话皱起眉头，然后耸了耸肩。“不知道。也许吧。我只是说有很多地方让人进来，我猜。而且何止如此——就在前几天，我们这帮兄弟差点一头撞上一伙兽人，他们正在那些废弃的牛头人宅邸里翻找，把看到的东西全都抢走。我是说，我们当然能打，但我们只是猎人。那些灰皮绝对不是这一带的，过去来劫掠的兽人大多是绿皮。 ”老实说，没了牛头人维持秩序，现在这里就是一场混战。不过既然你从山上大老远下来，这对你来说应该不算意外，对吧？“ 海岸地带还有当地人留在附近吗？我是说从以前就在的，不是那些跑来趁乱打劫的？ ”有些鹰身女妖吧，我猜，虽然她们现在脑子不太正常了。“那只佩克西加斯特指着海边的悬崖。”我们几个想吃海鸥蛋，正准备开始往上爬，那些鹰身女妖就一副要把我们团团围住的样子。我们一下子就没什么胃口了。 “她们住在崖壁的洞里，一向有点脾气酸，但现在她们的程度是过去的五倍、十倍。不知道她们出了什么事，也不想知道；只要我们待在沙滩上，她们就不来烦我们。但你——我猜搞清楚这些事就是你的工作，不然你也不会问这些问题，对吧？也许你要是能把她们打醒，鹰身女妖能告诉你的比我们多。”

rows.original:
Those are all the questions you have for now; you won't bother them on their hunt, then.
    
    "Good chat. We were a bit worried when you showed up, but it all worked out, didn't it? It's nice to have someone to talk to who's got [pc.hisHer] head put on right. This is just bad all around, and we've got to stick together."
    
    He's right. Even though the demons have retreated from the gates of Khor'minos, the coastlands are still overrun with all kinds of danger — not just from the demons or tainted, but all kinds of opportunists in the bargain. Well then, you'll be on your way, then.
    
    The pexighast bobs his head, half-turns to rejoin his tribesmen, then pauses. "Look, we lads kind of busy right now with this big 'un, so we're keeping it short. We'll be coming back every day, so long as the hunting's good; catch us while we're taking a break and we'll have a lot more going on. Since you've been beating down some of the crazies along the cliffs and beach so we don't have to, a bit of hospitality from us sounds pretty fair, right?"
    
    Sounds good — having someone to watch your back while you take a breather isn't the worst of propositions. You'll consider that offer the next time you bump into them.
rows.translation:
这些就是你目前所有的问题了；那就不打扰他们狩猎了。
    
    “聊得愉快。你出现的时候我们还有点担心，但结果一切都好，对吧？能跟一个[pc.hisHer]脑子摆得正的人聊天真好。这世道到处都糟透了，我们得抱成一团。”
    
    他说得对。尽管恶魔已经从科尔米诺斯的城门前撤退，海岸地带仍然充斥着各种危险——不只来自恶魔或腐化者，还有趁机而入的各种投机分子。那么，你该上路了。
    
    那只佩克西加斯特晃了晃脑袋，半转过身要回到族人身边，然后又停住了。“你看，我们这帮兄弟现在忙着处理这大家伙，所以就长话短说。只要狩猎还行，我们每天都会回来；趁我们休息的时候找上我们，我们能聊的就多得多。既然你一直在悬崖和海滩边揍那些疯子，省得我们动手，那我们招待你一下也算挺公道，对吧？”
    
    听起来不错——在你歇口气的时候有人替你看着背后，这提议不算最差的。下次碰上他们时，你会考虑这个提议。

rows.original:
As you make your way along the grey-pebble beach, the familiar sight of the tribal pexighasts draws into view, all half-dozen of them. The lizardfolk greet you with calls and waves, although you note they don't take their attention off their surroundings, nor do they slacken their grip on their bone spears.
    
    "Good to see you again, friend," one of them says as he steps up. "There aren't many on this shore of late."
    
    And yet they keep on coming back.
    
    A shrug and grin. "What can I say? We lads need entertainment — just enough danger to kick us in the tail, not enough to actually kill. We're smart enough to stay away from the city by the bay, and besides, the hunting continues to be really good.
    
    "But since you showed up... we lads were about to take a breather ourselves, and [party.som
        |you
        |you and your friend
        |you and your friends
    ] would be welcome to join. Never hurts to have more pairs of eyes on watch while the others rest, especially those that're suited to being above the waves than below them. Want to join us?"
rows.translation:
当你沿着灰色卵石的海滩往前走时，熟悉的部落佩克西加斯特身影映入眼帘，六只全都在。这些蜥蜴人用呼喊和挥手向你打招呼，不过你注意到他们并没有把注意力从四周移开，也没有放松握着骨矛的手。
    
    “很高兴再见到你，朋友，”其中一只走上前来说道。“最近这片海岸上人不多。”
    
    可他们还是不停地回来。
    
    他耸了耸肩，咧嘴一笑。“我能说什么呢？我们这帮兄弟需要点乐子——危险刚好够踢我们尾巴一下，又不至于真把我们弄死。我们够聪明，会离海湾边那座城远远的，而且这里的狩猎一直都很不错。
    
    ”不过既然你来了……我们这帮兄弟正好也要歇口气，[party.som
        |你
        |你和你的朋友
        |你和你的朋友们
    ]愿意来一起坐坐。别人休息的时候多几双眼睛盯着总没坏处，尤其是那些更适合待在浪上而不是浪下的。要加入我们吗？“

rows.original:
As tempting as a respite from the constant danger of the coastlands might be, you have other places to be and things to do. Bidding the pexighasts farewell, you pass by them and are on your way; the last you see of the lizardfolk is them dragging together several pieces of driftwood into a circle of makeshift seats.
    
    Now then, you've other things ahead of you...
rows.translation:
尽管能暂时远离海岸地带那无休无止的危险着实诱人，但你还有别的地方要去，别的事情要做。你向佩克西加斯特们道别，从他们身旁走过，继续上路；……你最后看到的这群蜥蜴人，是他们正一起把几块浮木拖到一起，围成一圈当作临时座椅。
    
    那么，前方还有别的事等着你……
rows.raw:
"
    As tempting as a respite from the constant danger of the coastlands might be, you have other places to be and things to do. Bidding the pexighasts farewell, you pass by them and are on your way; the last you see of the lizardfolk is them dragging together several pieces of driftwood into a circle of makeshift seats.
    
    Now then, you've other things ahead of you...
    "

rows.original:
You'd be more than happy to join them; they're not wrong that there are far too few friends in the coastlands of late, and the prospect of a moment's respite is tempting, especially with company.
    
    "Glad to have your company. With the way you've been clearing out all kinds to and fro, we'll definitely feel safer with you around."
    
    You help the pexighasts drag together several pieces of driftwood into a circle as makeshift seats and take your weight off your legs; the rest join you and lounge around as lizards do, while one of their number keeps watch. [rand
        |No sooner are you seated that they pepper you with questions about what's been going on in Khor'minos and how things turned out — the pexighasts are aware of the evacuation of Khor'Elthos, the city's occupation by demons and the failed attempt to besiege the eastern gate of the mountain, but that's about it. 
        
        Their eyes widen at your tales of the siege as it happened within the mountain and some of them appear just a little disbelieving at the details you provide, but it's undeniable that your account matches up with what they know of the eventual breaking of the siege and retreat of what's left of the demons to the bay.
        
        "No wonder you haven't had any problems with all the tailworkers hanging around the coast. If you could send an army of demons packing, a handful of chumps here and there aren't a problem for you."
        
        [pc.isDK
            |For once, it's good to have your prowess recognized
            |Well, it was mostly the legions; you helped a little
        ].
        
        "If that's how you see it. And since you're that big of a deal, it's about time you took up watch for bit, [pc.raceCute]. Make us all feel that much safer, yeah?"
        |No sooner are you seated that the pexighasts decide that it's time for a snack — they bring out raw cuts of meat and fish wrapped in seaweed, to which they thoroughly rub in some kind of thick, sour-smelling sauce before biting with relish.
        
        It's understandable that the pexighasts don't cook their food, what with living underwater, and it isn't like there wasn't some basic preparation, but it's still eye-opening after a fashion to see them do it so casually. A couple of them offer you portions, but it's clear they're well aware of any reluctance on your part are are just teasing you — they're well acquainted with land-dwellers and their habits, after all.
        
        That being said, you're glad when your turn to keep watch comes up — the scent in the air has grown thick and acrid enough for your eyes to start watering. The pexighasts give you light-hearted slaps as you get up to have a reprieve from your reprieve, but don't push you any further.
        |The pexighasts are eager to tell you all about their lives when they're not having a grand time on the beach — they regale you with tales of their homes in a handful of sea caves not too far off their coast, their dealings with minotaurs when Khor'Elthos was still a thriving port town, their womenfolk who prefer to stay far from land, and the occasional run-in with siorcanna who've wandered in from colder waters.
        
        It's familiar in a strange way, that their lives and drives aren't too different from your average group of youngbloods to be found in all peoples of the Marches, even if being aquatic and only occasionally venturing on land does necessitate some changes. But by and large, the pexighasts are just people like anyone else; if Hawkethorne had a lake or something they'd fit right in with a little time to adjust.
        
        "Can't imagine what it must be like to be a big shot like you," one of them remarks. "We lads know this stretch of coast pretty well, but that's about the extent of it. Still, if things get any worse, we won't even have to go looking for excitement if the excitement comes to find us!"
        
        Speaking of excitement, have they spotted any newcomers under the waves, rather than above them? You haven't encountered that many truly aquatic demons, but then again you haven't put yourself in position to run into them.[var0| There was that time with the sunken jotun castle and all the other shenanigans in the rift, but Tollus' goons had filled with with breathable air, so that doesn't really count, does it?]
        
        The pexighasts discuss this amongst themselves in their sibilant language, and shake their heads one by one before giving their reply. "No. We lads wouldn't go out to hunt this far out if our homes were at risk."
        
        Makes sense — if nothing else, at least [var0
            |the coastlands are removed far enough from the rift that the conflict there hasn't spread that far
            |the troubles haven't spread underwater as well
        ]. The pexighasts are more than a little chatty, and by the time it's your turn to keep watch you're a little glad to have the reprieve from your reprieve.
    ]
    
    A couple hours pass without incident, and eventually you're rested and it's time to move on. The pexighasts give you friendly nods as you part ways, bundling themselves into a tight group as they continue their hunt down the gray shoreline.
    
    You should get moving, too...
rows.translation:
你很乐意加入他们；他们说得没错，近来海岸地带的朋友实在太少了，能歇上一会儿的念头也确实诱人，尤其还是有伴一起。
    
    “有你们作伴真好。看你们来来回回清剿了那么多杂碎，有你在旁边，我们肯定觉得安全多了。”
    
    你帮这些佩克西加斯特把几块浮木拖到一起围成一圈，当作临时座椅，然后让双腿卸下重量；其余人也加入进来，像蜥蜴那样懒散地趴着，其中一个则负责放哨。[rand
        |你刚坐下，他们就劈头盖脸地问起科尔米诺斯发生了什么、结果如何——这些佩克西加斯特知道科尔埃尔索斯已经疏散、城市被恶魔占领、围攻山东门的尝试也失败了，但也仅此而已。 
        
        听你讲起山体内部那场围城战的经过，他们都瞪大了眼睛，有几个人对你提供的细节还显得有点将信将疑，但不可否认，你的说法与他们所知的最终解围、以及残余恶魔退向海湾的情况完全对得上。
        
        “难怪海岸边游荡着那么多长尾巴的家伙，你却一点麻烦都没碰上。你要是能把一整支恶魔大军都打跑，那零零散散几个废物对你来说算什么。”
        
        [pc.isDK
            |偶尔有一次自己的本事被人认可，感觉倒也不错
            |唔，主要靠的是军团；你只是帮了点小忙
        ].
        
        “你要这么想也行。既然你这么了不起，那也该轮到你放会儿哨了，[pc.raceCute]。让我们大家更有安全感一点，怎么样？”
        |你刚一坐下，佩克西加斯特们就决定该吃点零食了——他们拿出用海藻裹着的生肉块和生鱼片，往上面厚厚实实地抹了一层气味酸臭的酱料，然后津津有味地咬了起来。
        
        佩克西加斯特不烹饪食物是可以理解的，毕竟他们生活在水下，而且这也不是完全没有经过基本处理，但看他们这么随意地吃，多少还是让人开了眼界。有几个人分了些给你，不过很明显，他们很清楚你心里有多不情愿，只是在逗你玩罢了——毕竟他们对陆上居民和他们的习惯再熟悉不过了。
        
        话虽如此，轮到你放哨时你还是很高兴的——空气里的味道已经浓烈刺鼻到让你的眼睛开始流泪。你起身去给这场休息放个假时，佩克西加斯特们轻松地拍了拍你，但也没有再勉强你。
        |佩克西加斯特们很渴望地跟你讲起他们在海滩上玩乐之外的生活——他们滔滔不绝地讲起自己安在离海岸不远的那几处海洞里的家、讲起科尔埃尔索斯还是繁华港口城镇时他们与弥诺陶洛斯的往来、讲起他们那些宁愿远离陆地的女眷，还有偶尔撞上从更冷水域游荡过来的希奥卡纳的经历。
        
        说来有种奇怪的熟悉感：他们的生活和追求，与霜冻边境各族里随处可见的一群普通年轻人并没有太大区别，尽管水生、只是偶尔上岸确实带来了一些必要的改变。但总的来说，佩克西加斯特和任何人都一样，不过是普通人罢了；要是鹰棘镇有座湖之类的地方，给他们一点时间适应，他们完全能融入其中。
        
        “真想象不出像你这样的大人物是什么感觉。”其中一个说道。“我们这些小子对这一带海岸熟得很，但也仅止于此了。不过，要是局势再糟下去，我们连找刺激都不用费劲了，刺激自己就会找上门来！”
        
        说到刺激，他们在水下——而不是水上——有没有发现什么新来的家伙？你还没遇到过多少真正水生的恶魔，不过话说回来，你也没把自己放到会撞上它们的位置上。[var0| 倒是有过沉没的约顿巨人城堡那一次，还有裂隙里那些乱七八糟的事，但托勒斯的爪牙把那里灌满了能呼吸的空气，所以那也算不上数，对吧？]
        
        佩克西加斯特用他们那嘶嘶作响的语言互相讨论了一番，然后一个接一个地摇头，才给出回答。“没有。要是我们的家受到威胁，我们这些小子也不会跑这么远来打猎。”
        
        有道理——至少，退一万步说，[var0
            |海岸地带离裂隙足够远，那边的冲突还没蔓延到这里
            |这些麻烦还没有蔓延到水下
        ]。佩克西加斯特话实在不少，等轮到你放哨时，你甚至有点庆幸能从这场休息里再喘口气。
    ]
    
    几个小时平安无事地过去了，最终你休息好了，也该继续上路了。分别时，佩克西加斯特友好地朝你点头，然后挤成一团，继续沿着灰色海岸线打猎去了。
    
    你也该动身了……
rows.raw:
"
    You'd be more than happy to join them; they're not wrong that there are far too few friends in the coastlands of late, and the prospect of a moment's respite is tempting, especially with company.
    
    "Glad to have your company. With the way you've been clearing out all kinds to and fro, we'll definitely feel safer with you around."
    
    You help the pexighasts drag together several pieces of driftwood into a circle as makeshift seats and take your weight off your legs; the rest join you and lounge around as lizards do, while one of their number keeps watch. [rand
        |No sooner are you seated that they pepper you with questions about what's been going on in Khor'minos and how things turned out — the pexighasts are aware of the evacuation of Khor'Elthos, the city's occupation by demons and the failed attempt to besiege the eastern gate of the mountain, but that's about it. 
        
        Their eyes widen at your tales of the siege as it happened within the mountain and some of them appear just a little disbelieving at the details you provide, but it's undeniable that your account matches up with what they know of the eventual breaking of the siege and retreat of what's left of the demons to the bay.
        
        "No wonder you haven't had any problems with all the tailworkers hanging around the coast. If you could send an army of demons packing, a handful of chumps here and there aren't a problem for you."
        
        [pc.isDK
            |For once, it's good to have your prowess recognized
            |Well, it was mostly the legions; you helped a little
        ].
        
        "If that's how you see it. And since you're that big of a deal, it's about time you took up watch for bit, [pc.raceCute]. Make us all feel that much safer, yeah?"
        |No sooner are you seated that the pexighasts decide that it's time for a snack — they bring out raw cuts of meat and fish wrapped in seaweed, to which they thoroughly rub in some kind of thick, sour-smelling sauce before biting with relish.
        
        It's understandable that the pexighasts don't cook their food, what with living underwater, and it isn't like there wasn't some basic preparation, but it's still eye-opening after a fashion to see them do it so casually. A couple of them offer you portions, but it's clear they're well aware of any reluctance on your part are are just teasing you — they're well acquainted with land-dwellers and their habits, after all.
        
        That being said, you're glad when your turn to keep watch comes up — the scent in the air has grown thick and acrid enough for your eyes to start watering. The pexighasts give you light-hearted slaps as you get up to have a reprieve from your reprieve, but don't push you any further.
        |The pexighasts are eager to tell you all about their lives when they're not having a grand time on the beach — they regale you with tales of their homes in a handful of sea caves not too far off their coast, their dealings with minotaurs when Khor'Elthos was still a thriving port town, their womenfolk who prefer to stay far from land, and the occasional run-in with siorcanna who've wandered in from colder waters.
        
        It's familiar in a strange way, that their lives and drives aren't too different from your average group of youngbloods to be found in all peoples of the Marches, even if being aquatic and only occasionally venturing on land does necessitate some changes. But by and large, the pexighasts are just people like anyone else; if Hawkethorne had a lake or something they'd fit right in with a little time to adjust.
        
        "Can't imagine what it must be like to be a big shot like you," one of them remarks. "We lads know this stretch of coast pretty well, but that's about the extent of it. Still, if things get any worse, we won't even have to go looking for excitement if the excitement comes to find us!"
        
        Speaking of excitement, have they spotted any newcomers under the waves, rather than above them? You haven't encountered that many truly aquatic demons, but then again you haven't put yourself in position to run into them.[var0| There was that time with the sunken jotun castle and all the other shenanigans in the rift, but Tollus' goons had filled with with breathable air, so that doesn't really count, does it?]
        
        The pexighasts discuss this amongst themselves in their sibilant language, and shake their heads one by one before giving their reply. "No. We lads wouldn't go out to hunt this far out if our homes were at risk."
        
        Makes sense — if nothing else, at least [var0
            |the coastlands are removed far enough from the rift that the conflict there hasn't spread that far
            |the troubles haven't spread underwater as well
        ]. The pexighasts are more than a little chatty, and by the time it's your turn to keep watch you're a little glad to have the reprieve from your reprieve.
    ]
    
    A couple hours pass without incident, and eventually you're rested and it's time to move on. The pexighasts give you friendly nods as you part ways, bundling themselves into a tight group as they continue their hunt down the gray shoreline.
    
    You should get moving, too...
    "

rows.original: While the pexighasts are getting settled in, you mention to them that you'd like to get down and dirty with them on the sand. An excited ripple runs through the lizardfolk and they chat excitedly amongst each other in their own tongue; eventually, one of the tribal pexighasts steps forward, all tattoos and muscles, and acknowledges you with a nod. "You want to wrestle?" Yes. "I'tll be a good fight. Let's go." Not much of a talker, huh? You set down your [pc.weapon] in the camp and follow your opponent out of the circle and onto the coarse gray sand. As the rest of the lizardfolk watch excitedly, he takes a stance a respectable distance from you and spreads his claws, inviting you to strike the first blow. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 趁着佩克西加斯特们安顿下来的工夫，你向他们提起，你想和他们在沙滩上好好滚上一场。蜥蜴人群中泛起一阵兴奋的骚动，他们激动地用本族的语言互相议论；最后，一名部落佩克西加斯特走上前来，满身刺青和肌肉，朝你点了点头。 “你想摔跤？” 想。 “这会是一场痛快的比试。来吧。” 话不多啊，是吧？你把[pc.weapon]放在营地里，跟着对手走出圈子，踏上粗糙的灰色沙地。其余蜥蜴人兴奋地围观着，他在离你一段体面的距离外摆开架势，张开双爪，邀你打出第一击。 开打！

rows.original: "Oh?" You point over the pexighast's shoulder at two of his fellows, who've broken away from your camp and are grappling with each other on the rocky beach. The two've set aside their weapons and are instead seeking to send the other to his feet, in addition to throwing the occasional punch — while there's genuine aggression there, there's also an element of grandstanding and they're clearly not intending to genuinely hurt the other. "Oh. Those two." The pexighast turns over his shoulder and yells something at the duo in their sibilant native language, to which he gets shouted replies in the same. Shaking his head, the pexighast gives you a toothy, apologetic grin. "Don't mind them, they've got too much energy and too little sense. Been having some kind of petty squabble since we left — honestly, it's better that they wrestle it out and get fucked than keep fuming the entire trip." Wrestle, he says? The pexighast tilts his head. "You don't have wrestling?" You understand the general concept, you're just a little curious as to how his tribe goes about it. "Don't know what there is to say. No weapons, punching, throwing. Maybe a little biting if things get rough, but we lads are usually smart enough to save that for afterwards. Usually." And afterwards... "Fucking. Make it clear who's come out on top and that there're no hard feelings afterwards. Why're you so interested, anyway? Thinking of having a go yourself?" Well... "If you want to waste your energy instead of taking a breather, I'm sure the lads will oblige — we've seen you beating on the thick-tails while coming down the cliffs, and wouldn't mind having some of that excitement for ourselves. And... there's the fucking afterwards. I'm sure they wouldn't mind trying some [pc.race] either, be it from the top or bottom — not many of your kind under the waves, so I'm sure the lads'll jump at the chance." And the fucking's an inseparable part of the wrestling. "Like I said, don't want any hard feeling afterwards, do you? No better way to prove it — I guess you don't have to if you win, but if you lose..." All right, you've heard enough. [party.randComp cait brint brienne kiyoko azyrran arona quintillus vivianne agni ryn |"Sounds pretty exciting, [pc.name]!" Cait pipes up from beside you. "It's like one of those matches the temple would host with the sacred harlots every year, only with a lot less perfume and oil, and a... well, the idea is the same, isn't it?" A lot less gleaming oil, and you daresay the pexighasts are a lot more naked than the sacred harlots ever were, given all the lizardfolk are wearing are a bunch of tattoos. But as she said, the heart of the matter is still the same. "Go for it if you're interested! I'll be rooting for you!" |"Sounds a lot like how we do wrestling in Khor'minos," Brint muses from his seat at your side. "Well, minus the fucking at the end — not that it doesn't happen, but it's usually more private." You can imagine. That being said, you don't remember wrestling being that big of a deal back during your stay in Khor'minos. A sheepish grin. "It's just how it is. Two bulls — or even heifers — oiled up and going at each other may be fun, but it doesn't draw the crowds the way a flooded colosseum and mock naval battle does." With how excited he's getting, he looks fit to have a go at wrestling the pexighasts himself. "What, and steal your thunder? You heard the man, he wants to see you fight." Brint grins. "I'd never upstage a [pc.mf |brother |sister ] like you, [pc.name] — go for it if you want, I'm happy resting my feet for a bit." |"Sounds a lot like how we do wrestling in Khor'minos," Brienne muses from her seat beside you. "Well, the part that comes after's private, but that's about it." Wrestling, huh? You'd have imagined it would be more popular in Khor'minos. "Everything is, really; when you get a big enough city there's always someone interested in something. Two heifers all oiled up and going at each other... well, now I understand it a little better, looking at it from the other side. The greatest minds of the city, the matrons who plan the roads and aquaeducts, teach the young — now grunting as they grope each other on the sands... there's a certain kind who finds that really hot. Not as popular as flooding the colosseum and having naval battles, but... you know." And has she ever been tempted? "Not when I'm with you, [pc.name]. Why don't you go and show these lizards what you're made of? I'll be rooting for you!" |"Oh, Beloved. I do not mind if you wish to engage in boxing with these fine lizards. If anything, it would be quite interesting." Interesting? Kiyoko tries to portray herself as ever-genteel; you wouldn't have figured [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |her ] for being one to be interested in what usually amounts to a lot of grappling and grunting. Or maybe she just wants to see you do that? "You misunderstand. While the lizardfolk do not have the bulk needed for something proper like, say sumo — which is primarily the provence of the tanuki for that reason — there's nevertheless a certain something or the other to it, is there not? "I confess, Komari was a big enthusiast of tanuki sumo when we were younger; I was so soft-hearted as to indulge her desires. Now, I am not saying that you ought to do anything, Beloved. But I do think it would be interesting, would it not?" |Azyrran's been listening to all of this at your side, her eyes trained on the pexighasts grappling atop the gray, stony sand. After watching the lizardfolk for a moment, she slowly claps once, twice, thrice. Ha. Is it that entertaining for her? "It'd be moreso if you went up there and had a bout, sweetie." And what about her? Wouldn't she rather wrestle herself? "We do that all the time back at the hive when some of my sisters get restless, so I understand where these lizards are coming from. If it's between seeing you throwing fists and doing it myself, I'd rather have the first." Does she just want to see you fuck some pexighasts? "The other way around's fine, too." |"Ha! Now that looks like fun," Arona says from beside you. "Are you going up, [pc.name]? Because if you aren't, I am. [arona.weapon] is fun enough, but I want to make sure I've still got it." The orcess grins toothily and cracks her knuckles, champing at the bit to get started already. With her being that eager, it's nice of her to let you have dibs on any wrestling bout. "Ah, I know I'll be fine — me fighting them would just be to blow off some steam. [arona.isDom |You, though? You could use the practice. |You, though...?" Yes? "I'll admit, I like seeing you fight, just under fighting with you at my side. It's not often that someone can consistently beat the Kervus, and... look, I just want to see you throw hands, okay?" Why, does it give her a stiffy or something? "No! ]" Does she want you to ask the pexighasts if they'd be willing to have a two-on-two match? "No! That'd be unfair. To them, I mean." Arona [arona.isDom |snorts |clears her throat with more than a hint of uncertainty ]. "Why're you making it out to be some big deal, anyway. Just throw hands if you want to!" |Beside you, Quin scratches his chin, the bunny-boy's eyes trained on the pexighasts grappling with each other. Observant and slightly bemused is how one could describe Quin as he finishes his assessment and turns to you. "They've surprisingly good form, don't they? All that despite almost certainly not being formally trained." Couldn't they have picked it up from the minotaurs? "Nah." Quin jabs a finger at the grappling lizardfolk. "These guys are slender, like me. They have to cut through the water, do a whole bunch of swimming. The minotaurs are a lot more heavyset and that changes everything when it comes to wrestling. The pexighasts just don't have the bulk for minotaur-style wrestling — whatever they're doing, it didn't come from Khor'minos, and honestly with the way they're moving I don't think it's even really suited for fisticuffs on land. "Frankly? The more I watch them, the itchier my fingers are getting — I think there's something I can learn from them. The sex afterwards, if it happens, that's a bonus. If you're not going to take them up on it, [pc.name], I will." |"Hmm." Watching the pexighasts go at it, Viv looks thoughtful as she scratches her chin. "Interesting. Would you mind going up against the pexighasts, [pc.name]?" Oh? "They move in a fashion that's subtly different from the more grounded subspecies of lizardfolk, and notably so when they're excited. Not surprising when they're more suited to swimming or walking, but would you be a dear and really excite them so they have to fall back on their instincts more?" Is there any particular reason, though? A shrug. "I just find it fascinating. Do I need any other reason?" |"Ah, to be young and have that much energy," Agni murmurs as she watches the pexighasts go at each other on the stony beach. "I wish I still did." Well, doesn't she? With how her body rejuvenates every life and all. "It's not a problem of the body. I know I've the energy somewhere in there — still feel a little awkward for jumping you right away when you brought me back." Agni sighs. "But sometimes in those quiet moments... I feel like far too little jam spread over far too much bread. The things I've forgotten, as well as what I've managed to remember... at times, I feel like I've wound up stretched pretty thin living all those lives, compared to these lizards. "Sorry about that. Go and throw some fists with these lizards if you want, I'll provide a little musical accompaniment if you do." |"It's interesting, isn't it?" You turn to find Ryn looking over at the pexighasts wrestling with each other, your elven companion looking slightly worried. What is? "Diplomacy. I was raised to believe it was a lot of people taking about serious matters, discussing state interests, and shuffling papers. And then I go out into the world with you, and —" A lot of it is who's boinking who? "Yeah. Whether it's a tribe of simple people or the minoan king himself. It's just not what I expected. Maybe it's what Alissa would have, but... I suppose for all her faults, she was smarter about other people." Hey, you didn't make the rules as to how the world works, but so long as they're in your favor you'll play by them. "And when they aren't?" That's why you keep her around. |As one, the rest of the pexighasts turn to you and give you toothy grins. "We're not going to push you into it, but there's no need to be shy, either. Whoever comes out on top in the end, everyone will learn a lot, isn't that right? The lads have seen you fight those thick-tails on the cliffs and coast, and we're all right impressed." They're not very subtle about cajoling you into a bout, either. "It's as it does." ] It can't have been more than a few minutes, but one of the wrestlers manages to get his arms around his opponent and send the other pexighast sprawling onto the coarse gray sand. A cheer goes up amidst the rest of the tribal lizardfolk, and it looks like the bout's coming to an end as the victor steps forward, tapered cock half-hard as it protrudes from his genital sheath. If you're going to step in, this would be the time. Would you like to wrestle? It'll be an experience, if nothing else, and if you have a thing for lizardmen...
rows.translation: “哦？” 你越过佩克西加斯特的肩头，指向他的两个同伴——他们已经离开你们的营地，正在多石的沙滩上互相扭打。那两人把武器丢在一边，一心要把对方摔倒在地，偶尔还会甩出一记重拳——那里面有真实的敌意，但也带着几分做戏的成分，显然他们并不打算真的弄伤对方。 “哦。那两个啊。”佩克西加斯特扭过头，用他们那嘶嘶作响的母语朝那两人喊了句什么，得到的也是同样语言的吼叫回应。他摇了摇头，朝你露出一个露齿的、带着歉意的笑容。“别管他们，他们精力过剩、脑子又不够用。我们出发以来他们就一直为点鸡毛蒜皮的事吵个不停——说实话，他们打一架、操一顿把火气发泄出来，总比一路上臭着脸强。” 摔跤，他是这么说的？ 佩克西加斯特歪了歪头部。“你们没有摔跤？” 你明白大概是什么意思，只是有点好奇他的部族是怎么摔的。 “不知道有什么好说的。不用武器，可以挥拳，可以摔。要是打急了也许还会咬上几口，不过我们这些小子通常够聪明，会把那个留到事后。通常吧。” 那事后呢…… “操逼。把谁占了上风讲清楚，事后谁也别记仇。不过你为什么这么感兴趣？想自己上场试试？” 这个嘛…… “你要是想不歇着、非要耗耗体力，小子们肯定乐意奉陪——我们看见你下崖的时候一路揍那些厚实尾巴了，也想来点那种刺激。而且……事后还有操逼。我敢说他们也不会介意尝尝[pc.race]的滋味，不管是在上面还是下面——水下可没多少你这样的，所以小子们肯定会抢着上。” 而操逼是摔跤不可分割的一部分。 “就像我说的，事后不想留什么芥蒂，对吧？没有比这更好的证明方式了——我想你赢了的话也不是非得做，但要是你输了……” 好吧，你听够了。 [party.randComp cait brint brienne kiyoko azyrran arona quintillus vivianne agni ryn |“听起来挺刺激的，[pc.name]！”凯特在你身旁插嘴道。“就像神殿每年都会跟圣妓们办的那种比赛，只不过香水味和油光少多了，而且……唔，精髓是一样的，对吧？” 油光确实少多了，而且你敢说，佩克西加斯特们比那些圣妓穿得还少——毕竟这些蜥蜴人就只有一身刺青。不过正如她说的，这件事的核心还是一样的。 “有兴趣就去嘛！我会给你加油的！” |“听起来很像我们在科尔米诺斯摔跤的方式，”布林特坐在你身旁沉思道。“只不过最后没有操逼那一段——不是说没有，只是通常比较私密。” 你能想象。话虽如此，你不记得自己在科尔米诺斯逗留期间，摔跤有那么重要。 他不好意思地笑了笑。“就是这样。两头公牛——甚至母牛——抹上油互相缠斗也许挺好玩，但它招不来满场观众，比不上灌满水的竞技场和模拟海战。” 看他这么兴奋，他看起来随时都能亲自上去跟佩克西加斯特们摔一场。 “怎么，抢你的风头？你也听见了，人家想看的是你打。”布林特咧嘴一笑。“我绝不会拆[pc.mf |兄弟 |姐妹 ]你的台，[pc.name]——想去就去吧，我正好乐意坐着歇会儿脚。” |“听起来很像我们在科尔米诺斯摔跤的方式，”布蕾妮坐在你身旁沉思道。“只不过后面那部分是私下的，其他都差不多。” 摔跤，嗯？你还以为这在科尔米诺斯会更流行一些。 “其实什么都流行；城市一大，总有人对什么感兴趣。两头母牛抹上油缠在一起……嗯，现在从另一面看，我倒是稍微理解了一点。城里最聪明的头脑、那些规划道路和水道、教导年轻人的主母们——如今在沙地上互相摸索着发出闷哼……就是有那么一类人觉得这特别带劲。不像灌满竞技场搞海战那么受欢迎，不过……你懂的。” 那她自己有没有动过心？ “跟你在一起的时候没有，[pc.name]。你不如上去让这些蜥蜴人看看你的本事？我会给你加油的！” |“哦，亲爱的。你想和这些好蜥蜴人比划拳脚，我并不介意。真要说的话，那会相当有趣。” 有趣？清子总是努力表现得端庄有礼；你没想到[kiyoko.married |你的狐妻 |她 ]会对这种基本上就是搂抱和闷哼的事感兴趣。又或者，她只是想看你去做这种事？ “你误会了。这些蜥蜴人没有足够魁梧的体格去做什么正经的玩意儿，比如说相扑——正因如此，相扑主要是狸猫的专长——但即便如此，这里面还是有那么点意思的，不是吗？ ”我承认，我们年轻的时候，麻里可是狸猫相扑的狂热爱好者；我心肠太软，就纵容了她的兴致。当然，我不是说你应该去做什么，亲爱的。不过我确实觉得那会很有意思，不是吗？“ |阿兹兰一直在你身旁听着这一切，眼睛盯着在灰色多石沙地上扭打的佩克西加斯特们。她看了一会儿这些蜥蜴人，然后慢慢地拍了一下手，两下，三下。 哈。这对她来说有那么好看吗？ ”要是你上去跟他们打一场，那就更好看了，甜心。“ 那她自己呢？她不是更愿意亲自上去摔一场吗？ ”在蜂巢里，我的姐妹们躁动起来的时候我们总这么干，所以我明白这些蜥蜴人的想法。要是在看你挥拳和亲自上场之间选，我更想看你上。“ rows.raw: " "Oh?" You point over the pexighast's shoulder at two of his fellows, who've broken away from your camp and are grappling with each other on the rocky beach. The two've set aside their weapons and are instead seeking to send the other to his feet, in addition to throwing the occasional punch — while there's genuine aggression there, there's also an element of grandstanding and they're clearly not intending to genuinely hurt the other. "Oh. Those two." The pexighast turns over his shoulder and yells something at the duo in their sibilant native language, to which he gets shouted replies in the same. Shaking his head, the pexighast gives you a toothy, apologetic grin. "Don't mind them, they've got too much energy and too little sense. Been having some kind of petty squabble since we left — honestly, it's better that they wrestle it out and get fucked than keep fuming the entire trip." Wrestle, he says? The pexighast tilts his head. "You don't have wrestling?" You understand the general concept, you're just a little curious as to how his tribe goes about it. "Don't know what there is to say. No weapons, punching, throwing. Maybe a little biting if things get rough, but we lads are usually smart enough to save that for afterwards. Usually." And afterwards... "Fucking. Make it clear who's come out on top and that there're no hard feelings afterwards. Why're you so interested, anyway? Thinking of having a go yourself?" Well... "If you want to waste your energy instead of taking a breather, I'm sure the lads will oblige — we've seen you beating on the thick-tails while coming down the cliffs, and wouldn't mind having some of that excitement for ourselves. And... there's the fucking afterwards. I'm sure they wouldn't mind trying some [pc.race] either, be it from the top or bottom — not many of your kind under the waves, so I'm sure the lads'll jump at the chance." And the fucking's an inseparable part of the wrestling. "Like I said, don't want any hard feeling afterwards, do you? No better way to prove it — I guess you don't have to if you win, but if you lose..." All right, you've heard enough.
